canonicalAudit.derivation: JCS escapes LF and the control scalar, leaves the accented scalar in UTF-8 and emits the surrounding JSON string quotes.
Compare UTF-16 code units: ASCII a precedes b, and the high surrogate D800 of U+10000 precedes E000.
Generic JCS uses ECMAScript shortest binary64 strings, the positive exponent sign, and zero for negative zero. This vector does not admit unsafe integral tokens into a profile.
Hash each explicitly authored UTF-8 allocation tuple with SHA-256, use all 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, and prefix g_. Definition ownership for Collaboration is explicit.
The raw key a and escaped key \u0061 decode to the same Unicode-valid key. R3.2 requires profile-json-duplicate-key before its colon, value or schema checks.
The decoded D800 code unit has no following low surrogate. R3.2 requires profile-unicode after string decoding and before schema validation.
The converted value of -0 is finite and safely integral. R3.2 admits it lexically; generic canonical identity renders it as 0. This bounded verdict does not claim full-profile schema acceptance.
The number token 1e400 converts to non-finite binary64. R3.2 requires profile-number before a following delimiter or any schema validation.
The token 9007199254740993 converts to binary64 9007199254740992, an integral value outside the inclusive safe range. R3.2 requires profile-number; the criterion is the converted value.
The schema integer domain is mathematical: 1.0 is finite, safe and integral. Both validators admit it and its canonical value is 1.
The value 1.5 is not mathematically integral. Both validators reject its integer type; the profile boundary uses profile-schema.
Full-string pattern matching rejects trailing LF in id. Stock search-based matching is retained only as the documented reference divergence, never as profile acceptance.
The closed 29-keyword subset omits format. The profile rejection is profile-schema-keyword; reference-specific ignore/throw outcomes remain documented, not substituted for it.
The compiled-options schema and its profile registry target are explicitly pinned inputs. Resolve the known reference from those bytes only; this reference fragment is valid.
The compiled-options reference has no supplied registry target in this case. Refuse profile-schema-ref; do not fetch it. The reference diagnostic is bounded comparator evidence.
Numeric severity 3 means info. The common adapter deliberately transports info as warn and restores effective info for both accept and draft policies.
The generic rule transports at error while each profile subrule keeps its effective severity. Draft readiness warning counts as warn and does not fail acceptance.
Missing factories and the specific unknown-lookup exception both map to a typed lint-config-unknown integrity refusal. They never silently disable a rule.

Depth-first allowlisted resolution encounters cycle/a then cycle/b then cycle/a. Preserve the two cycle members and refuse lint-config-cycle.
A relative filesystem escape is not one of the allowed extends forms. Reject configuration syntax before resolver execution.
Index Task_1 at its immutable native pointer, then escape tilde before slash for each supplied segment. The unresolved ghost retains unavailable provenance and null pointer.
Each evaluation uses its own compiled options and fresh linter state. The A to B to A sequence must restore the original A options without retaining B state.

localCoverage.recursiveDepth: Objects inside arrays, nested values and first sibling before next sibling.
localCoverage.postWalk: Lexical failures in the root beat trailing tokens. Trailing tokens are rejected without walking a second root. Non-JSON whitespace fails the final parse unless the walk already failed.
localCoverage.schemaBoundary: Each lexical code wins in otherwise schema-invalid input, including unknown nested fields. Lexically valid null reaches schema and is refused as profile-schema.
localCoverage.positiveScope: profile-lexical-parse only; no claim of full-profile schema acceptance.
localCoverage.sameKeyUnicodeDuplicate: A duplicate comparison requires a successfully decoded, Unicode-valid key. An unpaired-surrogate key already fails on its first occurrence; there is no reachable same-key Unicode/duplicate tie.
